subject: Teaches pre-formal relation typing for concept edges in graphs, maps, taxonomies, ontologies-in-sketch, and…

evals.prompt: Define semantic-relations in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the semantic-relations skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind semantic-relations. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.

A user asks: "I need formal OWL axioms, class restrictions, and reasoning semantics on a knowledge base". Should semantic-relations activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force semantic-relations onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to pattern-recognition, linguistics, semantic-center, conceptual-modeling, knowledge-modeling, ontology-modeling, taxonomy-design, entity-relationship-modeling.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "our codebase uses customer, client, buyer, and user in different modules -- which relation analysis tells us whether this is synonymy, near-synonymy, or distinct domain language?". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying semantic-relations.

Place semantic-relations among its adjacent skills (pattern-recognition, linguistics, semantic-center, conceptual-modeling, knowledge-modeling, ontology-modeling, taxonomy-design, entity-relationship-modeling). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about semantic-relations and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
